result.summary: Plain-English check of respond-2-runar-PR4557.html, sections Short version, 0, 1, 2, R1-R4 (verbatim reviewer quotes excluded). 40 findings, 0 must, 24 should, 16 nit. By rule: Rule 1 (define at first use) 18; Rule 2 (one claim per sentence) 10; Rule 3 (units and meaning, est. label) 2; Rule 4 (citation placement) 1; Rule 6 (idioms/jargon) 4; Rule 8 (short sentences, no semicolons) 8 (three findings count under two rules). Semicolons in prose outside code and citation brackets: one, in the R3 claims table. The four Proposed reply blocks (R1 98 words, R2, R3 99, R4) are first person ("I will ..."), contain no names and no @-mentions, and define their terms adequately for the reviewer. Word-count labels: R2 says 97 and R4 says 96, a whitespace split gives 98 and 99 (the operators "<", "%", "==", "0" count as tokens), not a plain-English rule. Most Rule 1 findings are terms defined later in the same section than their first use (AMX, CI, TPS, A/B band, KV head, FPGA); the fix is to move the definition to the first use. The recurring jargon "cold abort block" / "on the taken path" appears five times across section 1 and R2.

findings.section: R3 claims (row: The aligned parameter has never been validated anywhere)
findings.phrase: The bf16 and fp16 chunk loaders use the unaligned forms whatever the flag [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:63-92].
findings.what: Wrong fact. chunky<bf16, true> calls tron_mm_load_bf16, which auto.hpp:35 defines as _mm256_load_si256 (the aligned form) [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:49-53]. chunky<fp16, true> calls tron_mm_load_fp16, which auto.hpp:43 defines as tron_mm_load_bf16, also aligned [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:74-78]. Only the <bf16, false> and <fp16, false> specializations use loadu [chunky.hpp:62-66, 86-90]. So the flag selects aligned vs unaligned for bf16 and fp16 exactly as it does for float.
findings.fix: The bf16 and fp16 chunk loaders follow the flag the same way: the true specializations call tron_mm_load_bf16 / tron_mm_load_fp16, which auto.hpp defines as _mm256_load_si256, and the false ones call the loadu forms [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:49-92, h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:35-36, 43-44].

findings.phrase: The bf16 and fp16 chunk loaders use the unaligned form whatever the flag.
findings.what: Same wrong fact as in the claims table. chunky<bf16, true> and chunky<fp16, true> use the aligned 256-bit load (tron_mm_load_bf16 = _mm256_load_si256, tron_mm_load_fp16 = tron_mm_load_bf16); only the false specializations use loadu [h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:49-92, h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:35-36, 43-44].
findings.fix: For bf16 and fp16 chunk loads it does the same: the true specializations use the aligned 256-bit load and the false ones the unaligned load.
